_comment: Copy to council-agents.json (gitignored) and keep only the agents you actually run. The host takes the command ONLY from this file, never from the council record, so convening a council can never choose what executes on your machine.

host._doc: Loopback control channel for /council. port is the first tried; the host walks up to 8791 if it is taken. origins are ADDED to http://localhost:3000 and http://127.0.0.1:3000 - put your deployed PWA origin here to drive the council from it.

agents._doc: mode 'acp' means the host owns the agent over the Agent Client Protocol: one session for the whole council, turns pushed as session/prompt, and the MCP bearer token passed over stdio so it never lands on disk. mode 'shell' is the old one-process-per-turn behaviour and keeps its on-disk --mcp-config. Optional 'env' is merged over the host's environment for that agent only; an object value is JSON-stringified, for a vendor that takes its whole config in one variable. Optional 'warn' is surfaced on the agent's card in /council - use it for anything that makes this agent weaker than the others. VERIFY the command with `scripts/council-acp-probe.mts --agent <name> --prompt` before trusting it: these are config, not code, and the vendors move.
agents._doc_containment: The host path-checks fs/read_text_file, fs/write_text_file and any permission request carrying toolCall.locations, and forces terminal cwd to the worktree. An agent that does its own file IO is NOT covered by that gate: run the probe with --edit to find out which kind you have, and put a warn on the entry if it is the second kind. As of 2026-08-01 both codex and cursor are the second kind.
agents._doc_mcp_name: The host injects the council MCP server as 'zuychin-council' (COUNCIL_MCP_SERVER_NAME in src/lib/council/protocol.ts). Do not rename it to match a server the agent already has configured: codex-acp silently DROPS a requested server whose name already exists in its own config unless DISABLE_MCP_CONFIG_FILTERING=true, which leaves the agent authenticating against the wrong endpoint with no error.

claude-code._doc: VERIFIED 2026-07-31: `claude` itself has NO --acp flag; the ACP entry point is Zed's adapter, which wraps the Claude Code SDK. `npx -y @zed-industries/claude-code-acp` downloads it on first use; `npm i -g @zed-industries/claude-code-acp` then lets you use "command": "claude-code-acp" with no args.

codex._doc: VERIFIED 2026-08-01 in a live council. Not `codex acp`: the desktop build's codex.exe is Access denied from a shell, so this runs @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp (a devDependency here) by absolute path under node. Install it with `npm i -D @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` and point at your own checkout. ACP mode is what makes codex usable at all: `codex exec` auto-cancels MCP tool calls non-interactively (openai/codex#24135), and the only workaround was --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox. In ACP mode approvals come back through the host, so that flag is not needed - the live council ran without it. CODEX_CONFIG below only disables unrelated plugins, which caused memory pressure; the council MCP server arrives over session/new and needs no codex-side config.
codex.warn: writes files without calling fs/write_text_file and sends no toolCall.locations, so the host can neither see nor path-check its file access

cursor._doc: VERIFIED 2026-08-01 in a live council: `cursor-agent acp` serves ACP natively. `agent` is the same shim but too generic a name to claim on PATH. Needs spawnResolved - Node refuses to spawn the .cmd shim directly (CVE-2024-27980). ACP mode also sidesteps the print-mode bug where -p could hang without releasing the terminal.
cursor.warn: writes files without calling fs/write_text_file and without requesting permission at all, so the host can neither see nor path-check its file access

antigravity._doc: https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/headless - no --acp upstream yet, so this stays on the shell adapter and behaves exactly as it did before: one process per turn, prompt in argv, MCP config written outside the worktree because it holds a bearer token. --print-timeout defaults to 5m, far below a 90m council, so it is raised here. Shell commands are soft-denied headlessly unless allowed: add permissions.allow rules in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json (preferred) or append --dangerously-skip-permissions.
antigravity.warn: shell mode: no --acp upstream yet, so no permission mediation, no streamed activity and no turn dispatch - this agent long-polls its own turns
